LIVED CONSEQUENCE
RECEIPTS.

Show how a decision affected you through a redacted bill, notice, correspondence, service change or other lawful record—without pretending one receipt proves the whole outcome.

Privacy boundary: Raw submissions remain private in the protected contact intake queue. Public receipts require redaction, explicit publish consent and named human review. One receipt does not prove a general pattern or causation.

Submit safely

Describe the receipt before sharing sensitive material.

  • Remove names, account numbers, addresses, signatures, barcodes, QR codes and unnecessary metadata.
  • Do not submit information about children, medical details or another person’s private data through the ordinary form.
  • Do not upload stolen, hacked, unlawfully obtained or dangerous material.
  • For sensitive documents, use the site’s client-side PGP route rather than ordinary links.
